body.x: The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is an intergovernmental organization supporting its Member and Partner States to achieve environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive and economically resilient growth. In partnership with the Government of Luxembourg, GGGI is preparing the Climate Nexus Finance Facility (CNFF), a five-year global programme (2026–2030) with an estimated budget of EUR 20 million. The Facility aims to strengthen fiscal, financial and public investment frameworks to align financial systems with climate, nature and resilience objectives. Its work includes supporting Ministries of Finance and regulators, National Development Banks, public investment and public–private partnership systems, and the development of bankable climate-resilient and nature-positive investments. The Facility targets mobilization of USD 5 billion toward Climate Nexus objectives, alongside capacity building, investment frameworks, resilient infrastructure projects and climate risk insurance products.

Hiring and appointment to this position are conditional upon signature of the Contribution Agreement between GGGI and the Government of Luxembourg. The anticipated starting date is January 2027, subject to signature and entry into force of the agreement, confirmation of the approved staffing structure and budget, and completion of GGGI recruitment procedures. This Job Description does not constitute an employment commitment.

The Finance and Corporate Services (FCS) Associate will support financial management, budget monitoring, procurement and contract administration for the Climate Nexus Finance Facility (CNFF) and other GGGI Global Sustainable Finance Programs. As part of the Project Support Unit (PSU), the Associate will work closely with the Project Management Unit (PMU), Project Technical Unit (PTU), program teams and GGGI's corporate Finance and Procurement functions to ensure efficient program delivery, accurate financial records and compliance with GGGI policies and procedures. The role will also provide administrative and logistical support to the GGGI Luxembourg Office as needed.
Support effective financial and procurement management across CNFF and other Global Sustainable Finance Programs in accordance with approved budgets and GGGI policies and procedures.
Provide timely budget, expenditure and commitment information to support program implementation and management decisions.
Support transparent, timely and compliant procurement and contract administration.
Provide administrative and operational support to the GGGI Luxembourg Office as needed.
Coordinate with CNFF and other Global Sustainable Finance Program teams on budgets, procurement needs, contracts and implementation schedules.
Liaise with corporate Finance, Procurement, Legal and Human Resources on financial and administrative matters.
Guide program staff on financial procedures, documentation, timesheets and procurement requirements.
Coordinate with suppliers, consultants and service providers on contracts and administrative arrangements, including Luxembourg Office operational needs.
Help prepare annual budgets, PIN cost estimates, procurement plans, forecasts and budget revisions for review and approval.
Maintain budget-versus-actual and commitment trackers by project code, budget line and intervention; flag overspending, delivery delays and funding gaps.
Prepare and track requisitions, purchase orders, invoices and payment requests in GGGI’s ERP, checking completeness, coding, budget availability and required approvals.
Review personnel-cost allocations, timesheets, travel and consultant charges against approved assignments and eligible costs; maintain project-level traceability and flag potential double charging.
Coordinate procurement documentation, including technical teams’ terms of reference, specifications, cost estimates and solicitation inputs, with corporate Procurement.

Support solicitation administration, evaluation logistics, due-diligence documentation and contract preparation under applicable procedures; route decisions to authorized officials and preserve confidentiality and segregation of duties.
Track consultant and supplier contracts, commitments, deliverables, expiry dates and amendments; obtain technical acceptance and authorized approvals before submitting payment documentation.
Reconcile project financial trackers with ERP records and prepare financial inputs to donor reports and management updates with corporate Finance.
Maintain complete financial and procurement audit trails and support expenditure verification, internal reviews and the independent financial audit at Action closure.
Support orderly financial and contract closure and propose practical improvements to tracking tools and workflows.
Provide administrative and logistical support to the GGGI Luxembourg Office as needed, including coordination of office supplies, facilities, meetings, events and official visits.
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, procurement, economics or a related field.
Preferably at least four years of relevant experience in project finance, accounting, procurement or contract administration, including exposure to both finance and procurement processes.
Experience with budgeting, expenditure monitoring, financial reporting and supporting procurement or consultant contracting.
Experience in donor-funded programs or international organizations is desirable; familiarity with EU-funded actions is an advantage.
Strong Excel skills and experience with ERP or comparable financial-management systems.
Fluency in written and spoken English is required; knowledge of French is an asset.
Strong numerical skills and accuracy in reconciliations, coding, cost allocation and financial records.
Working knowledge of procurement documentation, contract administration and financial controls.
Ability to manage concurrent transactions and deadlines and identify compliance gaps early.
Sound judgment, discretion and understanding of conflicts of interest, confidentiality and segregation of duties.
Ability to coordinate office administration and logistical arrangements effectively, with strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Demonstrates GGGI’s values of Integrity, Excellence and Sustainability and actively supports its mission.
Maintains accountability, confidentiality and transparency and uses public resources responsibly.
Works respectfully and constructively with colleagues and partners across cultures, functions and time zones.
Shares information, supports colleagues and contributes to continuous improvement and organizational learning.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
